claims.text: NbTaTiZrV0.5 is a BCC high-entropy or refractory high-entropy alloy that exhibits a high-temperature strength plateau.
The yield-strength plateau in NbTaTiZrV0.5 extends approximately from 673 K to 1073 K.
Elevated temperature normally facilitates dislocation motion and causes strength to decrease.
Plastic flow in pure and dilute BCC metals is conventionally controlled by screw-dislocation motion through thermally activated double-kink nucleation.
Edge dislocations can be prevalent and dominant over screw dislocations in a BCC alloy with good high-temperature strength.
TEM and diffraction measurements can establish the relative prevalence of edge and screw dislocations.
High strength in BCC high-entropy alloys is governed predominantly by edge dislocations.
High hardness in BCC high-entropy alloys is governed predominantly by edge dislocations.
Edge dislocations in these alloys undergo thermally activated super-jogging at elevated temperatures.
Thermally generated super-jogs create strong pinning points that impede further dislocation glide.
Super-jog pinning counteracts thermal softening and maintains high yield strength.
Alloys dominated by edge dislocations will show less strength loss between about 673 K and 1073 K than alloys dominated by screw dislocations.
Screw-dislocation-dominated alloys will soften continuously as temperature increases.
Composition changes or post-processing heat treatments can controllably alter the relative prevalence of edge and screw dislocations.
Slight compositional changes can suppress edge-dislocation formation and favor screw-dislocation activity.
The proposed mechanism should apply broadly to chemically complex refractory or BCC high-entropy alloys.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to FCC high-entropy alloys or alloys dominated by nanotwinning.
Direct in situ evidence connecting edge-dislocation super-jogging to the yield-strength plateau is limited.
Short-range order or minor second phases may also influence the high-temperature strength plateau.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies testing to temperatures above 1073 K, whereas the conditions describe ramping only to approximately 1073 K.
